'''''Cattleya trianae''''' (Lind. & Rchb. fil),  also known as ''Flor de Mayo'' ("May flower") or "Christmas orchid",<ref>{{cite web |url=http://orchidlady.com/pages/orchidGarden/ChristmasPartTwo.html |title=The Christmas star orchid |accessdate=2010-07-04 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110728011844/http://orchidlady.com/pages/orchidGarden/ChristmasPartTwo.html |archivedate=2011-07-28 }}</ref> is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the family ''[[Orchidaceae]]''.<ref name=POWO>{{cite web |url= https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:622257-1 |title= Cattleya trianae Linden & Rchb.f. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=The Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=June 25, 2025}}</ref><ref name=COL>{{cite web |url= https://www.catalogueoflife.org/data/taxon/RWJ3 |title= Cattleya trianae Linden & Rchb.f. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Catalogue of Life |publisher=Species 2000 |access-date=June 25, 2025}}</ref> It grows as an [[epiphytic]] orchid, with [[succulent]] leaves, [[endemism|endemic]] to [[Colombia]] where it was nominated as the [[national flower]] in November 1936.  That year, the [[National Academy of History of Argentina]] asked the Latin American countries to participate in an exhibition with the representative flowers of each country.  The Colombian government gave the botanist [[Emilio Robledo]] the task to designate the most representative flowering plant of the country.

The choice of ''Cattleya trianae'' was made for two main reasons:

*The [[Labellum (botany)|lip]] is yellow, blue and red, in the same way as the Colombian flag.   
*The species was named after the 19th century Colombian botanist [[José Jerónimo Triana]].

The species grows at 1500–2000 meters above sea level, in [[Cloud forest]]s. It is an endangered species due to [[habitat destruction]].<ref>{{Cite journal| issn = 0034-7744| volume = 55| issue = 2| pages = 681–691| last = Franco| first = Marcela|author2=Giovany Guevara |author3=Neftali Mesa |author4=Gloria Urueña | title = Hardening of the national flower of Colombia, the threatened Cattleya trianae (Orchidaceae), from in vitro culture with previous invigoration phase| journal = [[Revista de Biología Tropical]]| accessdate = 2013-04-08| date = June 2007| url = http://www.scielo.sa.cr/scielo.php?pid=S0034-77442007000200031&script=sci_arttext&tlng=pt| doi = 10.15517/rbt.v55i2.6045| pmid = 19069780| doi-access = free}}</ref>

The [[diploid]] [[chromosome]] number of ''C. trianae'' has been determined as 2''n'' = 40. the [[haploid]] [[chromosome number]] has been determined as ''n'' = 20.<ref>page 251 of L. P. Felix and M. Guerra: "Variation in chromosome number and the basic number of subfamily Epidendroideae (Orchidaceae)" ''Botanical Journal of the Linnean Society'' '''163'''(2010)234—278.
